paragraphs.text: When I think about the printing press, I think it changed society very much, but maybe not so fast like people imagine.
Before Gutenberg made his press around 1450, books were copy by hand, so they were expensive and only rich people or the church can have them.
After the press, the cost go down and more books were everywhere, which means normal people start to read too.
But the change was slow in the beginning.
Most people still could not read, and it took maybe one or two centuries for literacy to really grow across Europe.
The big effect was that ideas could travel faster than before, for example the religious ideas of Martin Luther spread quick because they were printed many times.
So in my opinion the printing press was like a slow explosion.
The technology came in one moment, but the real change in how people think and share knowledge happened over many years, not over night.
